Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

peabiru 0.1.5

  • New function locate_facilities(): where to open new facilities among candidate sites, by maximal covering, location set covering, p-median or p-center, on the travel times from the demand points to the sites by any mode (those of travel_time_matrix(), or a table given in travel_times). Existing facilities count first. The models are solved by a greedy construction followed by vertex substitution, with no solver; the result has the new sites with what each adds, the potential of every candidate, the facility and travel time of every demand point, and a summary. See the article “Facility location”.
  • New function floating_catchment(): the two-step floating catchment area (supply per unit of demand at each demand point) and its enhanced form, with any of the decay functions of accessibility().
  • Credits: the Title and Description, the README and the package help page now state up front that the engine is a ‘Rust’ port of Conveyal’s ‘R5’ routing engine and that the functions are modelled on those of ‘r5r’ (Ipea), from whose ‘Java’ code the fare calculator and parts of the trip planner are translated; the reference of ‘r5r’ (Pereira et al., 2021) is cited; and the README says that peabiru is not affiliated with or endorsed by Conveyal, Ipea or the r5r team. No change in the code.

peabiru 0.1.0

Breaking changes

  • The first argument of every function that takes a network is now network (it was r5r_network). Calls that pass the network by position are not affected.
  • The arguments r5r_core (every function) and sample_size (isochrone()), which were accepted with a warning and ignored, are gone.

New functions

  • trip_options(), a multi-criteria trip planner: for each pair, the trips not dominated on total time, fare, transfers and minutes on foot (any subset) at each departure minute of the window, merged into options, with their legs in the format of detailed_itineraries(). Exact on its trip definition, fares compared soundly for any fare structure, and frequency-based routes boarded at their expected times (no random draws).
  • detailed_itineraries(): the legs of each trip with their geometry, the fastest trip or the alternatives (shortest_path = FALSE, suboptimal_minutes), all_to_all, drop_geometry, osm_link_ids and output_dir.
  • Fares: setup_fare_structure(), read_fare_structure(), write_fare_structure(), and fare_structure and max_fare in travel_time_matrix(), accessibility() and detailed_itineraries(), routed with the multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR); pareto_frontier().
  • Network inspection: find_snap(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf(), check_transit_availability() and get_gtfs_errors().

New arguments and inputs

  • Public transport by specific modes ("BUS", "RAIL", …), and bicycle or car access and egress (mode, mode_egress, max_bike_time, max_car_time).
  • output_dir in the matrix functions, accessibility() and detailed_itineraries(): one CSV file per origin (or pair), routed and written a slice at a time.
  • Scenarios: new_carspeeds (by ‘OpenStreetMap’ way or by polygon), carspeed_scale and new_lts (by way or by line).
  • Elevation: a .tif raster in the data directory gives walking and cycling slope costs (elevation = "TOBLER" or "MINETTI"), in EPSG:4326 or the coordinate systems used for Brazil and worldwide whose transform is reproduced exactly (SIRGAS 2000, SAD69, Corrego Alegre and their UTM zones, SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic, WGS 84 / UTM, Pseudo-Mercator). Where the pixel a street point falls in depends on the last bits of the projection, peabiru reads the same pixel on every machine, with a warning; voids and values beyond +/-3276.7 m are stored wrapped around, with a warning.
  • ‘GTFS’ feeds with missing optional columns, short times or empty dates are read, and so is GTFS-Flex locations.geojson; feeds with errors of priority "HIGH" are refused (and get_gtfs_errors() lists the errors).

Changes

  • isochrone(): when sf::st_make_valid() with spherical geometry (s2) changes the area of a polygon by more than one part in 10,000 (it can, by several per cent, in polygons of many parts and holes), the polygons of that origin are repaired on the plane instead, with a warning of class peabiru_isochrone_repair. options(peabiru.isochrone_repair = "spherical") keeps the spherical repair.
  • The class of the tables returned is chosen by options(peabiru.output = ), read at each call: "tibble" (the default), "data.frame" (what every function returned before) or "data.table" (sf data.tables for isochrone polygons, itineraries, street edges and transit routes; an index on found in find_snap()). It applies to every table, sf results and the tables of fare structures and of trip_options() included. ‘tibble’ is now imported; ‘data.table’ stays suggested.
  • An sf of points (origins, destinations, points) or of scenario polygons or lines (new_carspeeds, new_lts) in another coordinate reference system than WGS 84 is reprojected with sf::st_transform(), with a message of class peabiru_reprojected naming the argument and the CRS (it was an error). An sf without a CRS is an error that says how to set it. Results stay in EPSG:4326.
  • read_fare_structure() keeps the columns of a table without rows in the file (it returned a table without columns).
  • Arguments are checked with the checks and messages of ‘checkmate’ and ‘cli’ (ported, without the dependencies).
  • The error for exactly 200 Monte Carlo draws with fares has class peabiru_200_draws.
  • Isochrone polygons follow the C++ library ‘isoband’ is built with on each platform, so that on each system they are the polygons ‘isoband’ gives there.
  • Street edge lengths are computed with a translation of Apache Commons Math’s FastMath, the same on every platform.
  • Park-and-ride areas link to the first vertex of the street edge they meet.
  • detailed_itineraries() follows rides along GTFS shapes cut by shape_dist_traveled, and plans car egress through turn restrictions with two or more via ways in a fixed order (that of a freshly built network), with a warning naming the pairs whose itinerary another order would change (both were errors).
  • write_fare_structure() deflates the archive.
  • What peabiru does not do “is not supported by peabiru” (no “yet”).
  • Under R CMD check with its limit on cores (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_), the default n_threads = Inf uses two threads instead of all cores.
  • The reference documentation describes each function on its own terms; new articles on itineraries, elevation, scenarios and inspecting a network. The article “Compared with r5r” says what the package shares with r5r, what differs and how to move a script over.

peabiru 0.0.1

  • First release: build_network(), travel_time_matrix(), accessibility(), expanded_travel_time_matrix(), arrival_travel_time_matrix() and isochrone().
